_comment: Hand-made mapping from Frama-C EVA's alarm kinds to SEI CERT C rule ids
and CWE ids. EVA has no rule ids: a check id here is EVA's own alarm
text as tcb/tools/frama_c.py normalises it ('out of bounds read',
'precondition of memcpy'), stable under the pinned Frama-C 33.0. Every
entry is a judgement about the defect the alarm asserts cannot happen,
made by reading the alarm's ACSL predicate, and the harness records this
file's sha256 into every run so a table can say which version of the
judgement it used. A kind with no entry and no matching pattern is
reported as `unmapped` -- counted, never dropped. `cert: []` means CERT C
has no rule for the defect; `cwe: []` likewise.
EVA's memory-validity alarms (\valid, \valid_read) fail for a null
pointer as much as for an out-of-range one, so they carry CWE-476; they
do not carry CWE-690, which the other mappings keep for checks that mean
specifically an unchecked allocation result. Where an alarm spans several
Juliet CWEs every one it can report is listed, because the Juliet tables
match a finding to a CWE directory exactly.
Precondition alarms name the callee whose ACSL contract a call may break;
the patterns group callees by what the contract protects. A callee not in
a group (printf-family varargs, fclose, sigaction, ...) stays unmapped
because its precondition mixes unrelated properties.
Add entries with a `note` saying why; change one only with a note saying
what was wrong.

patterns.note: a copy/fill/concatenate call whose destination or source range is not valid for the size
a stream call whose buffer is not valid for the size given
a compare/search call whose range is not valid to read for the size
a call whose string argument may not be a valid, null-terminated string
absolute value of the most negative integer
a math function called outside its domain or with a non-finite argument

out of bounds write.note: \valid(p) fails on a store: past either end, or null

out of bounds read.note: \valid_read(p) fails on a load: past either end, or null

accessing out of bounds index.note: an array index outside the declared bounds, read or write

signed overflow.note: signed arithmetic past either limit; as cppcheck integerOverflow, CWE-680 not listed

signed downcast.note: conversion to a narrower signed type that loses the value

accessing left-value that contains escap.note: read of a pointer to freed memory or to a local whose lifetime ended (\dangling)

precondition of free.note: \freeable(p) fails: already freed, not from an allocator, or not the start of the block

precondition of realloc.note: realloc of a pointer that is not freeable

unaligned pointer creation.note: a pointer converted to a type with stricter alignment

overflow in conversion from floating-poi.note: float to integer conversion out of range

non-finite double value.note: an operation produced an infinity or NaN

invalid LHS operand for left shift.note: left shift of a negative value; as clang-analyzer BitwiseShift

invalid RHS operand for shift.note: shift by a negative amount or by at least the width

pointer comparison.note: relational comparison of pointers into different objects

pointer subtraction.note: subtraction of pointers into different objects

pointer to function with incompatible ty.note: a call through a function pointer whose type does not match the callee

partially overlapping lvalue assignment.note: assignment between partially overlapping objects (C11 6.5.16.1p3); CERT C has no rule for it

trap representation of a _Bool lvalue.note: a _Bool object holding a value other than 0 or 1
